status: Exploratory. All three families and their original test outcomes were previously inspected. This freeze prevents undisclosed within-run edits; it does not turn them into confirmation data.
question: Do finite non-Blackwell-ordered source channels and two-step decision value improve acquisition on existing real retrieval traces?
changed_assumption: Backend identity is hidden from every selector and router, unlike the milestone's known-backend experiment. Each held-out family has four source worlds: the other two corpora crossed with BM25/dense. No claim of direct superiority over the known-backend setup.
model: Uniform prior over four worlds. For each world, fit a five-outcome ordinal RR-difference distribution in eight family/action channels from deduplicated source probes; Dirichlet pseudocount 0.5 per outcome. Bucket action utility uses only source train rows, shrunk with 8 pseudo-queries to that world's global mean. Source-average bucket frequencies weight acquisition. Missing short-probe coverage remains an extrapolation limitation.
independence_limit: Likelihood factorization is uncalibrated. Select at most one contrast per equal family/bucket/query-feature group to reduce shared-original correlations; groups may merge coincident feature vectors. Cross-question and cross-document dependence remains. Tempered likelihood power 0.25 is a prespecified sensitivity check.
lookahead_limit: Receding two-step planning scores expected terminal source utility, divided by first-probe search cost. It plans at channel level and may optimistically assume a second channel remains available after removing the selected question group. It is a heuristic, not exact finite-pool optimal planning.
comparators: RRF over all five action rankings
controls: cyclically rotate source utility matrices relative to source likelihoods
costs: Matched maximum search-call budgets. Every positive budget charges all pool sampling and generation plus actually selected retrieval calls. Serving costs reported separately. Fixed original/keywords use one search and no LLM. Semantic/HyDE use one search and one shared-format generation. Decomposed uses two searches and one generation. RRF all-actions uses six search calls and the same one generation, not three generations. Offline source training/retrieval cost is separate and inherited from milestone.
statistics: Paired query/seed resampling, descriptive 95% intervals within each environment. Three families are not enough for a population-level significance claim. Report all conditions/budgets; no cherry-picked primary win.
fresh_family_gate: Advance this particular acquisition model to untouched families only if development shows a positive macro improvement over both random and IG, action changes in at least two families, and gains surviving strong fixed/RRF comparisons. Otherwise diagnose before consuming fresh targets. This is an engineering gate, not a statistical publication threshold.
primary_development_comparison: standard lookahead2 at 64 maximum search calls; equal mean across three families and both backends, vs standard random and information_gain at64. All other budgets/conditions descriptive.
